extracted.intended_audience: general readers and people interested in humor, folkloristics, or popular-culture joke forms
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for composing or recognizing 'yo mama' / 'your mom' jokes, including their typical structure, common targets, variants, and cultural functions/risks. Focused on the specific joke form rather than humor generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening formula / incipit
rubrics_metrics.description: Your mom jokes usually consist of a sentence that starts with 'Your mother...' (or equivalents like 'yo mama' or 'your mom').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opening phrase signals the genre immediately; the phrase 'yo mama' by itself, without qualifiers, has become commonly used as an all-purpose insult or expression of defiance. Slang variants such as 'ur mum' are sometimes used depending on speaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derogatory target categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The insulting statement typically targets the mother's behavior, appearance, social status, or intelligence ('...is so fat...', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common targets include promiscuity and obesity, but the form's limit is human ingenuity — insults may concern any attribute that exploits norms of parental respect. Authors should choose a specific target category to anchor the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration + punchline by implausibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The derogatory statement is often illustrated with an example which pushes the content into implausibility, providing the punch line of the joke (e.g., '...she looks at the menu and then says to the waiter: Okay.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective jokes create an exaggerated, absurd example that makes the target's trait ludicrous. The illustrative anecdote converts a claim into a surprising, concrete image that carries the humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit/allusive variant (omission of explicit insult)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absurd statements can follow directly after the beginning of the joke, whereby the explicit insult (fat, ugly, poor, stupid) is omitted and only implicitly resonates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers may rely on cultural allusion or unusual phrasing ('Your mother's name is Ottfried and she is the bull of Tölz') to evoke qualities without naming them; subtlety or cultural reference can be used instead of blunt assertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-sentence narrative build-up
rubrics_metrics.description: More unusual variants consist of several sentences which initially tell a more complex story but later boil down to the same punchline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer setups can add misdirection and context, increasing payoff when the final line reframes earlier material as evidence of the insult. Keep cohesion so the ending reads as an ironic collapse of the story into the insult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogic/interplay/outdoing format
rubrics_metrics.description: Yo mother jokes can be designed as an interplay of insults that tie in with each other in dialogue and outdo each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in back-and-forth exchanges (e.g., 'Fuck yourself' / 'I'm tired from fuckin' your wife' / 'How's your mother?' ... ), this format relies on escalation and callbacks; timing and rhythm matter to land the back-and-forth punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-contexts and genre conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Insults involving 'your mother' are commonly used when playing the Dozens, in battle rap, juvenile culture, and as punchlines in movies and stand-up routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators should choose conventions appropriate to context: Dozens and battle-rap expect competitive escalation; stand-up and film may use yo mama jokes as quick character beats or established comic shorthand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural/linguistic variants and register
rubrics_metrics.description: Slang variants and local forms exist (e.g., 'ur mum'); in non-American areas the association can be with juvenile culture generally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of regional phrasing, register, and audience expectations; what reads as playful in one dialect/community may be taken as highly offensive in another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social function (expressing or mitigating anger)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dozens was a way to express or mitigate anger in underprivileged African-American groups; the form has social/gender implications within matriarchal structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators and analysts should recognize that yo mama jokes often serve interpersonal functions (venting, bonding, status play) beyond mere nastiness; understanding function informs tone and acceptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk and potential consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Compared to other types of insults, 'your mother' insults are especially likely to incite violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should be aware of real-world risks when using this form; its high potential to provoke conflict affects where and how it is appropriate to deploy such jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical continuity and precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: The form has historical precedents across cultures (ancient examples cited: Rabbi Eliezer, Plutarch's anecdotes, Strategies of the Warring States).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using historical motifs or classical allusions can lend depth or irony to a modern yo mama joke; however, historical referencing may shift the joke toward commentary rather than straightforward insult.
